title: Compatibility confidence levels and onboarding checklist
creator: Aisha Karim
description:
Problem statement: New open-model submissions to the catalog arrive with uneven maturity signals (docs missing, flaky tokenizer behavior, unknown kernel/ops incompatibilities). PMs and runtime engineers need a deterministic, lightweight way to decide whether a new model can be: (A) accepted as an immediately supported catalog entry, (B) accepted behind a soft-pin / experimental flag, or (C) rejected and returned with a remediation checklist. This ticket clarifies the acceptance criteria, defines a compatibility confidence scale, and produces a concise onboarding checklist that runtime and QE can use to gate intake.

Goals: (1) Define a 3-level compatibility confidence taxonomy (High / Moderate / Low) and mapping to onboarding actions (full entry / soft-pin + canary / hold-for-remediation). (2) Specify the minimum runtime sanity checks and artifacts we require for each level (model card, tokenizer mapping, reproducible inference script, basic perf profile). (3) Define the soft-pin behavior: what runtime variants are allowed, how automatic fallback is triggered, and which telemetry/alerts must be enabled while soft-pinned. (4) Produce a one-page onboarding checklist and a minimal PRD-style acceptance table for catalog UI and ingestion automation.

Out of scope: detailed quantization recommendations, deep performance optimization work, or changing the existing pin/fallback implementation; those will be separate follow-ups after this ticket produces the gating contract and checklist.
acceptance_criteria: A three-level compatibility confidence taxonomy exists with clear, measurable signals for High / Moderate / Low and a short justification paragraph for each.
A mapping table that ties confidence level => onboarding action (e.g., High=>catalog entry, Moderate=>soft-pin with canary, Low=>reject+remediation) is documented and reviewed by runtime and QE.

Minimum artifact checklist for each level is enumerated: required files (model card, sample input/output traces), reproducible inference script (docker or script), tokenizer mapping, and at least one smoke test that reproduces tokens across variants.

Soft-pin operational contract is defined including: telemetry required (per-request lat/err, token mismatch alerts), canary rollout percentage guidance, allowed runtime variants, and automatic fallback triggers (5xx rate, latency SLO breach, token-diff threshold).
A one-page onboarding checklist (Google Doc link) and a JSON schema snippet for automated intake validation are attached to this ticket.
Runtime and QE engineers have signed off on the checklist in comments or via an approval PR referenced in this ticket.
Front-end/ingest team has confirmed the required metadata fields exist in the catalog intake form (or accepts a small enhancement follow-up tracked under dependencies).
decisions: Adopt three confidence levels (High/Moderate/Low) rather than a wider numeric scale to keep intake lightweight and reduce reviewer ambiguity.
Moderate confidence models will be admitted behind a soft-pin for at least two weeks with strict telemetry before being eligible for full catalog promotion.
Low confidence models are rejected from automated ingestion and returned to contributors with a remediation checklist; exceptions require an explicit cross-team approval and a parent_issue reference.
notes: Proposed telemetry thresholds: 5xx > 1% over 1 hour => immediate rollback; median latency increase > 2x baseline over 30m => pause canary; token-diff > 0.5% on evaluated prompts => create accuracy regression alert.

Suggested minimal smoke tests: (1) run 10 canonical prompts and compare top-3 token sequences across variants, (2) verify tokenizer roundtrip for UTF-8 edge cases, (3) synthetic throughput test to ensure KV cache behavior is stable.
UI/ingest fields needed: model_provenance, tokenizer_name+version, reproducible_inference_link, declared_quantization_options, soft_pin_flag. If missing, file a follow-up with FE/ingest.
